title: CurAItion Story Candidate Handoff (click-bait-scout variant)
description: A story-candidate handoff from a live-web scout. SUPERSET of the standard story-candidate contract: every field a renderer already reads is preserved, so this validates as a drop-in wherever the standard shape is accepted. Adds a `mode` discriminator, a per-candidate `virality` block, and source-credibility fields. For click-bait, the primary `the_signal_24h.citations` MUST be live web sources (WebSearch/web_fetch) inside the 24h window; any CurAItion facts are optional and live in `the_depth_90d` / `curaition_crossref`.

mode.description: Discriminator so renderers can adjust tone (urgent/topical vs evergreen/curious). click-bait-scout always emits 'click-bait'.

window.description: For click-bait, fresh_hours is a HARD filter (default 24, max 48 for a still-accelerating story).

depth_days_min.description: Only relevant when a CurAItion depth layer is attached.

scope_verification.description: OPTIONAL for click-bait (web-first). Populate ONLY if CurAItion was queried as a cross-reference; proves the library-only scope held. Omit entirely on a pure-web run.

curaition_used.description: false on a pure-web run; true if CurAItion cross-ref was called

headline_hypothesis.description: The punchy, screenshot-ready angle in one line. Not a final headline.

domains.description: Contexts/domains this signal spans (news, politics, markets, crypto, sport, tech, entertainment, internet_culture, etc.). 2+ is the stronger case.

the_signal_24h.description: The live story. For click-bait, citations MUST be web sources inside the freshness window.

metrics.description: outlet count, platform spread, search-interest/share deltas, exact figures from the story, etc.

promotional_flag.description: true if the source is a press release / promo dressed as news — should lower rank

content_id.description: Optional; present only for CurAItion-sourced items.

outlet.description: Publisher/source name — used by the two-source corroboration rule.

published_at.description: Timestamp; must fall inside the freshness window.

virality.description: click-bait-specific signal block. The reason this scout exists.

virality_signal.description: How fast + wide it is spreading right now (Velocity/spread score).

source_velocity.description: Human-readable spread, e.g. 'covered by 6+ outlets in 8h; trending on X & Reddit'.

platforms.description: Where it is spreading: x, reddit, tiktok, news_wires, youtube, etc.

corroboration.description: multi-source (2+ independent reputable outlets) is REQUIRED for selection.

brand_safety.description: sensitive = tragedy/private individuals → handle soberly; unsafe = hoax/defamation/exploitative → cannot be selected.

freshness_hours.description: Hours since the story broke/spiked. Must be <= window.fresh_hours_max.

the_depth_90d.description: OPTIONAL CurAItion depth layer — the slow build behind today's spike. The signature move that beats a pure-news take.

curaition_crossref.description: OPTIONAL. Result of the 'do we already track this?' check. Omit on a pure-web run.

why_now.description: Causal hypothesis for the spike — what tripped it in the last 24h.

why_it_matters.description: Interpretive lift, explicitly derived from the cited facts above.

surprise_factor.description: The hook — what makes a reader stop and click/share.

suggested_formats.description: Shape the story wants to be, NOT the tool that renders it. Use the four canonical keywords: longform (a written argument), thread (a short sequence of posts), carousel (image slides), digest (a multi-item newsletter). The trailing longform-post/tweet-thread/carousel-producer values are DEPRECATED aliases retained so handoffs written before 2026-07-27 still validate — do not emit them. Naming formats rather than tools is what lets any renderer consume this handoff without that renderer having to exist when the handoff was written.

selected_candidate_id.description: The top pick: corroborated (multi-source), brand_safety != unsafe, inside the freshness window.
